stem:
Lichens are found growing on trees, walls, rocks and soil.

Fig. 9.1 shows a lichen of the genus Usnea. Usnea can tolerate only low concentrations of sulfur dioxide and does not grow in places where the air is polluted with sulfur dioxide.

{{figure:figure_9_1.webp}}

Fig. 9.1

Usnea is composed of a mixture of two types of cell:

- photosynthetic cells that are classified in the kingdom Protoctista
- fungal cells that are classified in the kingdom Fungi.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline the characteristic features of the kingdoms Protoctista and Fungi.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Xanthoria is a lichen that can grow in places where there is a high concentration of sulfur dioxide in the air, for example in towns where homes, factories and vehicles burn fuels.

Fig. 9.2 shows a lichen of the genus Xanthoria.

{{figure:figure_9_2.webp}}

Fig. 9.2
parts.text:
A student planned a method to measure the relative abundance of Usnea and Xanthoria on trees along a transect from the town centre at $0\text{ km}$ to unpolluted countryside at $4\text{ km}$.

Suggest why measuring the relative abundance of the two types of lichen gives information that is useful for conservation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Although a large biodiversity of lichens can be found in a range of habitats, most people ignore them.

Outline why forms of life that are usually ignored, such as lichens, should be conserved.
